evidence: Verg. A. 1.738–739: ille impiger hausit spūmantem pateram
terms.comment: The verb for drawing water, used of drinking a cup off at a draught. For greedy guzzling see “guzzle”; for drinking a cup to the last drop, “drain”.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica et post Augustum: Lucr., Verg., Ov. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Big gulps are largī haustūs, sips exiguī haustūs.

phrases.latin: Nōlī tam avidē haurīre; paulātim bibe.
phrases.english: Don’t gulp it down like that; drink it slowly.

phrases.latin: tum Bitiae dedit increpitāns; ille impiger hausit spūmantem pateram, et plēnō sē prōluit aurō
phrases.english: then she handed it to Bitias with a challenge; he promptly gulped down the foaming bowl and drenched himself from the brimming gold

phrases.latin: saepe, sed exiguīs haustibus, inde bibī
phrases.english: I have often drunk from it, but in small sips

sources: Lewis & Short: haurio · Lewis & Short: haustus
